en.content: In 3d series, the metal having the highest M2+/M standard electrode potential is :

options.content: Cr
Fe
Cu
Zn

en.explanation:
Cr+2/Cr –0.90 V

Fe+2/Fe –0.44 V

Cu+2/Cu +0.34 V

Zn+2/Zn -0.76 V

So Ans. is Cu+2/Cu

The 'f' orbitals are half and completely filled, respectively in lanthanide ions :

[Given : Atomic no. Eu, 63; Sm, 62; Tm, 69; Tb, 65; Yb, 70; Dy, 66]

options.content: Eu<sup>2+</sup> and Tm<sup>2+</sup>
Sm<sup>2+</sup> and Tm<sup>3+</sup>
Tb<sup>4+</sup> and Yb<sup>2+</sup>
Dy<sup>3+</sup> and Yb<sup>3+</sup>

en.explanation:
Tb 4f9 6s2

Tb+4 4f7

Yb 4f14 6s2

Yb+2 4f14

Hence, the pair Tb+4 and Yb+2 have half filled and completely filled f subshells respectively.

C. [MnCl6]3 (high spin)

D. [Mn(CN)6]3

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.content: A < B < D < C
B < D < C < A
A < C < D < B
B < D < A < C

en.content: Which of the following is most stable?
en.explanation: 1,3-cyclohexadiene is most stable because it is a neutral molecule. All others are intermediates and hence less stable.
